<!--
Updated for Rceattle >= 5.10.0. What changed, and what it means for the ESP
indices this document writes:

* `quantities$ration` is now `quantities$consumption_at_age` (the annual ration
  of ONE fish, kg/yr) and `quantities$biomassByage` is
  `quantities$biomass_at_age`. Both old names now resolve to NULL.
* Population-level consumption is `consumption_at_age * avgN_at_age`, not
  ration x biomass. The old formula multiplied by weight-at-age twice (it was a
  direct port of the ADMB `biomassByage * ration2`, where ration2 is a RELATIVE
  ration in g/g). The corrected ration index is therefore lower than the 2024
  index by roughly the consumption-weighted mean weight-at-age: about 10% for
  pollock and arrowtooth, about 4x for Pacific cod. Flag this in the ESP
  submission -- it is a units fix, not a change in the model.
* `plot_*()` return ggplot objects, so figures are saved with `ggsave()` and
  annotated with layers; `jpeg()` / `dev.off()` / `mtext()` / `legend()`
  chains no longer work.
* In `plot_m_at_age()` and `plot_ration()`, colour separates the MODELS and
  line type separates the SEXES. `lty` used to key on the model.
* `M_at_age` and `B_eaten_as_prey` are REPORTed but no longer ADREPORTed, so
  the fit carries no standard errors for them (`plot_m_at_age(add_ci = TRUE)`
  says the same thing). The uncertainty block below reports NA rather than a
  number the model never produced.
* `fit_mod()`'s `phase` / `verbose` arguments moved onto `fit_control()`; see
  "GOA_25 fit models.R".
-->

```{r echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(Rceattle)
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)
library(writexl)

# Load models and code
source("ESP_Figure_Code.R")
source("ESR_Figure_Code.R")
load("Models/GOA_25_mod_list.RData")

# Get model objects for use below
#  [[1]] single-species, fixed M   [[2]] single-species, estimated M
#  [[3]] multi-species
ss_model         <- mod_list_all[[1]]
ceattle_esr_model <- mod_list_all[[3]]

# Years come from the model rather than a literal, so a rerun with another
# terminal year does not need this document edited.
years  <- ceattle_esr_model$data_list$styr:ceattle_esr_model$data_list$endyr
thisYr <- years[length(years)]
nyrs   <- length(years)

spnames <- ceattle_esr_model$data_list$spnames   # Pollock, Arrowtooth flounder, Cod
nspp    <- ceattle_esr_model$data_list$nspp
nsex    <- ceattle_esr_model$data_list$nsex
nages   <- ceattle_esr_model$data_list$nages

# Uncertainty of key parameters
#
# `M_at_age` and `B_eaten_as_prey` are REPORTed but their ADREPORT lines are
# commented out in ceattle.cpp, so `sdrep` holds nothing for them. Earlier
# versions of this document pulled the sd straight out of `sdrep$sd`; that now
# matches zero elements and errors. Return an NA array instead, so the terminal
# values below are still reported and the missing uncertainty is visible rather
# than silently invented.
sdrep_array <- function(model, name, template) {
  hit <- which(names(model$sdrep$value) == name)
  if (length(hit) != length(template)) {
    warning(name, " is not in the sdreport (it is REPORTed, not ADREPORTed): ",
            "reporting NA for its standard error.", call. = FALSE)
    return(array(NA_real_, dim = dim(template), dimnames = dimnames(template)))
  }
  array(model$sdrep$sd[hit], dim = dim(template), dimnames = dimnames(template))
}

b_eaten_as_prey    <- ceattle_esr_model$quantities$B_eaten_as_prey
b_eaten_as_prey_sd <- sdrep_array(ceattle_esr_model, "B_eaten_as_prey", b_eaten_as_prey)

M_at_age    <- ceattle_esr_model$quantities$M_at_age
M_at_age_sd <- sdrep_array(ceattle_esr_model, "M_at_age", M_at_age)


# Mortality rates and means/peaks
#
# Two levels of summary, kept in separate objects. `mort` is one row per
# species x sex (age-1 M and the age-1 biomass eaten); `pred` is one row per
# species (biomass eaten and ration, summed over sex). The old script wrote both
# into the same vectors, so the per-sex arrowtooth entries were overwritten by
# the per-species totals.
mort <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nspp), function(sp) {
  do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nsex[sp]), function(sex) {
    M_ts <- ceattle_esr_model$quantities$M_at_age[sp, sex, 1, 1:nyrs]
    data.frame(
      Species           = spnames[sp],
      Sex               = if (nsex[sp] == 1) "Combined" else c("Female", "Male")[sex],
      peak_M            = max(M_ts),
      peak_M_year       = years[which.max(M_ts)],
      avg_M             = mean(M_ts),
      terminal_M        = M_ts[nyrs],
      terminal_M_sd     = M_at_age_sd[sp, sex, 1, nyrs],
      terminal_Age1_Beaten    = b_eaten_as_prey[sp, sex, 1, nyrs],
      terminal_Age1_Beaten_sd = b_eaten_as_prey_sd[sp, sex, 1, nyrs],
      stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  }))
}))

pred <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nspp), function(sp) {
  be     <- ceattle_esr_model$quantities$B_eaten_as_prey[sp, , , 1:nyrs, drop = FALSE]
  be_tot <- apply(be, 4, sum)                       # over sex and age
  be_a1  <- apply(be[, , 1, , drop = FALSE], 4, sum) # age 1 only, over sex
  ration <- weighted_ration(ceattle_esr_model, spp = sp, endyr = thisYr, minage = 4)
  data.frame(
    Species              = spnames[sp],
    avg_Beaten           = mean(be_tot),
    terminal_Beaten      = be_tot[nyrs],
    avg_Age1_Beaten      = mean(be_a1),
    terminal_Age1_Beaten = be_a1[nyrs],
    avg_Ration           = mean(ration),
    terminal_Ration      = ration[length(ration)],
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
}))

# Percent change in age-1 mortality between the peak and the terminal year
mort$prcnt_change <- round(abs(100 * (mort$terminal_M - mort$peak_M) / mort$peak_M), 2)

# Format some values for inline reporting
comma <- function(x) format(round(x, 0), scientific = FALSE, big.mark = ",")

avg_Beaten           <- comma(pred$avg_Beaten)
terminal_Beaten      <- comma(pred$terminal_Beaten)
avg_Age1_Beaten      <- comma(pred$avg_Age1_Beaten)
terminal_Age1_Beaten <- comma(pred$terminal_Age1_Beaten)
```

```{r chunk3, echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, include=FALSE}
sclr <- 1

cols <- nmfspalette::nmfs_palette("oceans")(3)[3:2]
mod_names <- c("Single-spp CEATTLE", "Multi-spp CEATTLE")
ss_ms <- list(ss_model, ceattle_esr_model)

# The plot_*() functions return ggplot objects. Save with ggsave() rather than
# jpeg()/dev.off(); the model legend is drawn by the plot itself, so the old
# legend() / mtext() calls are gone.
#
# The package theme puts the legend along the bottom. plot_m_at_age() draws two
# guides there (model colour and sex line type), which run off a 4.5-inch
# figure side by side, so stack the guide boxes instead. Only the box layout is
# touched: the plotters already drop a guide that has one level, and forcing
# `guides()` here would put those single-entry legends back.
save_fig <- function(plot, file, width = 4.5, height = 5) {
  if (inherits(plot, "ggplot")) plot <- plot + theme(legend.box = "vertical")
  ggsave(file, plot = plot, width = width * sclr, height = height * sclr,
         units = "in", dpi = 350)
}

# Figure 1: Time series of biomass
save_fig(
  plot_biomass(ss_ms, line_col = cols, species = 2, model_names = mod_names,
               ylab = "Age-1+ biomass (million mt)"),
  "Results/ATF_ESP_Fig1.jpg", height = 3.5)

# Figure 2: Time series of mortality
# Colour separates the models; line type separates female (solid) from male
# (dashed) arrowtooth -- `lty` keyed on the model before Rceattle 5.x.
for (a in 1:3) {
  save_fig(
    plot_m_at_age(ss_ms, age = a, species = 2, line_col = cols,
                  model_names = mod_names, lty = c(1, 2)),
    paste0("Results/ATF_ESP_Fig2_age", a, ".jpg"))
}

# Figure 3: Time series of biomass consumed
save_fig(
  plot_b_eaten(ceattle_esr_model, line_col = cols[2], species = 2),
  "Results/ATF_ESP_Fig3.jpg")

# Figure 4: Time series of annual ration
save_fig(
  plot_ration(ceattle_esr_model, line_col = cols[2], species = 2, minage = 4),
  "Results/ATF_ESP_Fig4.jpg")

# Figure 5: Combined plots
for (sp in seq_len(nspp)) {
  stub <- c("Pollock", "ATF", "Cod")[sp]
  save_fig(
    ESP_plot(msModel = ceattle_esr_model, ssModel = ss_model,
             age = 1, minage = 4, endyr = thisYr, species = sp),
    paste0("Results/", stub, "_ESP_Fig5.jpg"), height = 8)
}
```

# Indices

```{r echo=FALSE, eval=TRUE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}

# Annual biomass of GOA Pacific cod consumed by predators
# Annual biomass of GOA pollock consumed by predators
# Annual ration of GOA Pacific cod
# Annual ration of GOA pollock
# Total natural mortality (m1+m2) of age-1 GOA Pacific cod
# Total natural mortality (m1+m2) of age-1 GOA pollock

# -- Pollock and cod (both sex-combined: nsex == 1)
for (sp in c(1, 3)) {

  spname <- spnames[sp]

  Matage1 <- data.frame(
    Year = years,
    MS_M = ceattle_esr_model$quantities$M_at_age[sp, 1, 1, 1:nyrs],
    SS_M = ss_model$quantities$M_at_age[sp, 1, 1, 1:nyrs])

  Biomass <- data.frame(
    Year = years,
    SS_Biomass = ss_model$quantities$biomass[sp, 1:nyrs],
    SS_SSB     = ss_model$quantities$ssb[sp, 1:nyrs],

    MS_Biomass = ceattle_esr_model$quantities$biomass[sp, 1:nyrs],
    MS_SSB     = ceattle_esr_model$quantities$ssb[sp, 1:nyrs])

  # Summed over age (and over sex, which is one level for these two species)
  B_eaten <- data.frame(
    Year = years,
    Biomass_eaten_as_prey = apply(
      ceattle_esr_model$quantities$B_eaten_as_prey[sp, , , 1:nyrs, drop = FALSE], 4, sum))

  # Population consumption in mt/yr: individual ration x average numbers-at-age
  Ration <- data.frame(
    Year = years,
    Age4plusTotal = weighted_ration(ceattle_esr_model, spp = sp, endyr = thisYr, minage = 4),
    Age1plusTotal = weighted_ration(ceattle_esr_model, spp = sp, endyr = thisYr, minage = 1))

  # Indices to share
  write_xlsx(
    list(Age1_M  = Matage1,
         Biomass = Biomass,
         B_eaten = B_eaten,
         Ration  = Ration),
    paste0("Results/GOA ", thisYr, " ", spname, " ESP Indices.xlsx"))
}


# -- ATF (two sexes, so M and consumption are reported by sex)
atf <- 2

Female_M <- cbind(
  data.frame(Year = years),
  as.data.frame(t(ceattle_esr_model$quantities$M_at_age[atf, 1, 1:nages[atf], 1:nyrs])),
  data.frame(M = ss_model$quantities$M_at_age[atf, 1, 1, 1:nyrs]))
colnames(Female_M) <- c("Year", paste0("Multi-spp M Age_", 1:nages[atf]), "Single-spp M")

Male_M <- cbind(
  data.frame(Year = years),
  as.data.frame(t(ceattle_esr_model$quantities$M_at_age[atf, 2, 1:nages[atf], 1:nyrs])),
  data.frame(M = ss_model$quantities$M_at_age[atf, 2, 1, 1:nyrs]))
colnames(Male_M) <- c("Year", paste0("Multi-spp M Age_", 1:nages[atf]), "Single-spp M")

B_eaten_F <- apply(ceattle_esr_model$quantities$B_eaten_as_prey[atf, 1, , 1:nyrs, drop = FALSE], 4, sum)
B_eaten_M <- apply(ceattle_esr_model$quantities$B_eaten_as_prey[atf, 2, , 1:nyrs, drop = FALSE], 4, sum)

Ration_F <- weighted_ration(ceattle_esr_model, spp = atf, endyr = thisYr, minage = 4, sex = 1)
Ration_M <- weighted_ration(ceattle_esr_model, spp = atf, endyr = thisYr, minage = 4, sex = 2)

# Indices to share
write_xlsx(
  list(Female_M = Female_M,
       Male_M   = Male_M,

       Biomass = data.frame(
         Year = years,
         SS_Biomass = ss_model$quantities$biomass[atf, 1:nyrs],
         SS_SSB     = ss_model$quantities$ssb[atf, 1:nyrs],

         MS_Biomass = ceattle_esr_model$quantities$biomass[atf, 1:nyrs],
         MS_SSB     = ceattle_esr_model$quantities$ssb[atf, 1:nyrs]),

       B_eaten = data.frame(
         Year = years,
         Biomass_eaten_as_prey_F     = B_eaten_F,
         Biomass_eaten_as_prey_M     = B_eaten_M,
         Total_biomass_eaten_as_prey = B_eaten_F + B_eaten_M),

       Ration = data.frame(
         Year = years,
         Age4plusFemale = Ration_F,
         Age4plusMale   = Ration_M,
         Age4plusTotal  = Ration_F + Ration_M)),
  paste0("Results/GOA ", thisYr, " ATF ESP Indices.xlsx"))
```
